results.label: evicted-single
results.prompt: How do I list all evicted pods?

message.content:
To list all evicted pods in a specific namespace, you can use the following command:

```sh
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep Evicted
```

This command searches for pods that have been evicted across all namespaces. If you want to list evicted pods in a specific namespace, replace `--all-namespaces` with `-n <namespace>`:

```sh
kubectl get pods -n <namespace> | grep Evicted
```

Replace `<namespace>` with the actual namespace name.

results.label: concurrent-rollout
results.prompt: How do I check deployment rollout status and view logs in namespace demo? Include oc and kubectl examples.

message.content:
To check the rollout status of a deployment in the `demo` namespace, you can use either `oc` or `kubectl`. Both tools provide similar functionality.

### Using `oc` (OpenShift Client)
```sh
oc rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```
Replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment. This command will wait until the deployment is fully rolled out.

### Using `kubectl` (Kubernetes Client)
```sh
kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```
Similarly, replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment. This command will also wait until the deployment is fully rolled out.

### Viewing Logs
To view logs for a deployment in the `demo` namespace, you can use either `oc` or `kubectl`.

#### Using `oc`
```sh
oc logs deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```
Replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment. This command will show the logs for the first container in the deployment.

#### Using `kubectl`
```sh
kubectl logs deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```
Replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment. This command will also show the logs for the first container in the deployment.

### Prerequisites
- Ensure you have the necessary permissions to view deployments and logs in the `demo` namespace.
- Ensure that the deployment exists in the `demo` namespace.

These commands provide a straightforward way to monitor the deployment rollout status and view logs, which are essential for troubleshooting and maintaining applications in Kubernetes.
